blind_reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), including zero whenever consistent with the following inequality, assume
\[
2q+1<d.
\]
Everything defined below is fixed by this pair \((d,q)\). There are no further hypotheses. In particular, \(q\geq0\), \(d\geq2q+2\), and \(d>0\). Put \(r=q+1\), using the same number as an integer dimension and its usual real embedding in scalar formulas. Thus \(r\geq1\).

The index set \(\operatorname{Fin}(d)\) is \(\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), and \(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\) is \(\{0,\ldots,q\}\). Let
\[
D=\mathbb R^d,\qquad E=\mathbb R^{q+1},\qquad
\Omega=\{\omega:\{0,\ldots,q\}\longrightarrow\mathbb R^d\}.
\]
Both Euclidean spaces carry their Euclidean norms and Borel measurable structures; \(\Omega\) carries the finite product measurable structure. For any such Euclidean space \(V\), write \(\gamma_V\) for its centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance. The probability measure on \(\Omega\) is
\[
\mu=\bigotimes_{b=0}^{q}\gamma_D.
\]
The probability experiment is therefore to draw \(q+1\) independent standard Gaussian vectors \(\omega(0),\ldots,\omega(q)\) in \(\mathbb R^d\). Equivalently, writing \(\omega_{b,i}\) for coordinate \(i\) of vector \(\omega(b)\), one draws the \((q+1)d\) independent real standard Gaussian coordinates \(\omega_{b,i}\), with \(0\leq b\leq q\) and \(0\leq i<d\).

Define the deterministic real threshold and coefficient
\[
L=2(q+1)+3\log(1000d)
\]
and
\[
a=\frac{1}{q+1}
  \int_{\mathbb R^{q+1}}
     \mathbf 1_{\{y:\|y\|_2^2\leq L\}}(x)\,\|x\|_2^2
     \,d\gamma_E(x).
\]
Here \(\log\) is the natural logarithm, and
\(\|x\|_2^2=\sum_{b=0}^{q}x_b^2\).
The indicator makes the scalar integrand equal to \(\|x\|_2^2\) when \(\|x\|_2^2\leq L\) and equal to zero otherwise. The boundary is included. This formula defines a particular canonical number \(a\) from \(d\) and \(q\); \(a\) is not an arbitrary input, a supplied certificate, or an additional assumption. Its integral is with respect to a separate standard Gaussian variable in \(E\). All integrals in this statement are Bochner integrals under the supplied convention that the integral is totalized to zero outside complete or integrable cases. The displayed scalar definition is a fixed definition, not a separately stated integrability hypothesis or conclusion.

For every coordinate index \(i\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), define
\[
\theta_i=\frac{(i+\tfrac12)\pi}{d}.
\]
Define a deterministic real vector \(t_i\) indexed by \(k\in\{0,\ldots,q\}\) by
\[
(t_i)_k=
\begin{cases}
1,& k=0,\\
\sqrt{2}\cos(k\theta_i),& k\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\pi\) is the usual circle constant, and \(\sqrt{2}\) is the nonnegative square root of \(2\). Indices appearing in these scalar formulas are embedded from natural numbers into real numbers.

For each \(i\) and each outcome \(\omega\), form the row vector
\[
g_i(\omega)=(\omega_{0,i},\omega_{1,i},\ldots,\omega_{q,i})\in E,
\qquad
s_i(\omega)=\|g_i(\omega)\|_2^2
            =\sum_{b=0}^{q}\omega_{b,i}^2.
\]
The coordinate wrapping and unwrapping in the packet merely regard this coordinate function as a Euclidean vector and recover the same real coordinates. Define the random matrix \(Y_i(\omega)\) of size \((q+1)^2\times(q+1)^2\), with rows and columns indexed by pairs in \(\{0,\ldots,q\}\times\{0,\ldots,q\}\), by
\[
Y_i(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac1d\bigl(g_i(\omega)g_i(\omega)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)
                   \otimes\bigl(t_i t_i^{\mathsf T}\bigr),
     & s_i(\omega)\leq L,\\
0,&s_i(\omega)>L.
\end{cases}
\]
The zero in the second branch is the zero matrix. For coordinate vectors \(u,v\), the outer product \(uv^{\mathsf T}\) has entry \(u_bv_c\) in row \(b\), column \(c\). The Kronecker product uses the following order of paired indices: if \(A\) and \(B\) have indices in \(\{0,\ldots,q\}\), then
\[
(A\otimes B)_{(b,k),(c,\ell)}=A_{b,c}B_{k,\ell}.
\]
Scalar multiplication by \(1/d\) multiplies each matrix entry. Consequently the complete entry formula, for every \(b,c,k,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,q\}\), is
\[
\bigl(Y_i(\omega)\bigr)_{(b,k),(c,\ell)}
 =\frac1d\,
   \mathbf 1_{\{\omega:\sum_{j=0}^{q}\omega_{j,i}^2\leq L\}}(\omega)
   \,\omega_{b,i}\omega_{c,i}(t_i)_k(t_i)_\ell.
\]
Thus the random outputs specified by the proposition are the \(d\) matrices \(Y_i\), each obtained by setting its entire outer-product matrix to zero when its own row norm squared exceeds \(L\).

The conclusion is the conjunction of these two assertions:

1. For every \(i\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), the function \(Y_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{(q+1)^2\times(q+1)^2}\) is integrable with respect to \(\mu\). In the supplied meaning, it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and has finite integral of its extended norm, where the finite complete real matrix space uses the Euclidean operator norm. Equivalently, the norm condition is
   \[
   \int_\Omega \|Y_i(\omega)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,d\mu(\omega)<\infty.
   \]
   This is an asserted conclusion, not a premise.

2. For every \(i\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), its Bochner integral is exactly
   \[
   \int_\Omega Y_i(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)
      =\frac{a}{d}\left(I_{q+1}\otimes t_i t_i^{\mathsf T}\right),
   \]
   where \(I_{q+1}\) is the identity matrix on the first, Gaussian-coordinate index. In coordinates, for every \(b,c,k,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,q\}\), this says
   \[
   \int_\Omega
      \bigl(Y_i(\omega)\bigr)_{(b,k),(c,\ell)}\,d\mu(\omega)
      =\frac{a}{d}\,\delta_{b,c}\,(t_i)_k(t_i)_\ell,
   \]
   where \(\delta_{b,c}=1\) when \(b=c\), and \(\delta_{b,c}=0\) otherwise. The explicit integrability conclusion ensures that this displayed matrix integral is an actual integrable expectation.

Both assertions range over every coordinate index \(i\) for each admissible pair \((d,q)\). They are deterministic statements about the functions and their integrals under the specified product measure, rather than a sample-dependent success claim. They do not assert that the displayed expectation equals the sampled matrix, nor state a concentration bound, a success probability, or a conclusion about a sum of the matrices.

All normalizations and constants are fixed: \(r=q+1\), the threshold has coefficients \(2\), \(3\), and \(1000\), the feature normalization is \(\sqrt2\), the Gaussian truncated second moment is divided by \(q+1\), and both the sampled matrix and its expectation have the factor \(1/d\). There is no unspecified constant or certificate dependence. The objects \(D,E,\Omega,\mu,r,L,a,\theta,t,g,Y\) depend only on \(d,q\), their indicated indices, and (where applicable) the outcome \(\omega\). The coefficient \(a\) is common to all \(i\).

The literal natural-number quantification permits \(q=0\). In that case the only feature index and Gaussian-vector index are zero, \(r=1\), the assumption is \(1<d\), \((t_i)_0=1\), and \(Y_i\) is the one-by-one matrix with entry
\[
\frac1d\,\mathbf 1_{\{\omega:\omega_{0,i}^2\leq 2+3\log(1000d)\}}(\omega)
\,\omega_{0,i}^2.
\]
The same two conclusions apply, with expectation the one-by-one matrix \([a/d]\) and with \(a\) given by the stated one-dimensional canonical Gaussian integral. Values \(d=0\) and \(d=1\) satisfy no instance of the hypothesis, so they yield no additional cases.

approved_definition_context: Fin n is the finite index set of natural numbers less than n. Natural numbers embed into real numbers in the usual way.

EuclideanSpace real (Fin n) is real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. WithLp.toLp 2 wraps a real coordinate function as that vector; WithLp.ofLp recovers the same coordinates.

stdGaussian on a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space is the centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance. Measure.pi is the finite product measure with the product measurable structure.
Set.indicator s f equals f on s and zero outside s. Real.log is the natural logarithm and Real.sqrt is the nonnegative square root.

Matrix m n real is a finite real matrix. Matrix.vecMulVec u v has entries u_i times v_j. Matrix.kronecker A B has paired indices and entry A_(i,k) times B_(j,l) at ((i,j),(k,l)). The symbol 1 is the identity matrix and scalar action multiplies every entry.

Matrix integrals use the Euclidean operator norm on the finite complete real matrix space. Integrable f mu means almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the extended norm; it is an asserted conclusion wherever displayed.

The integral notation is the Bochner integral. It is totalized to zero outside complete or integrable cases; the explicit Integrable conclusions require genuine integrability. All local lets define fixed objects, rather than additional assumptions.

assumptions: Let \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), and \(r=q+1\). Thus \(d\ge2\), \(r\ge1\), and \(q=0\) is retained.

The original outcome space is \(\Omega=(\mathbb R^d)^r\), with the literal product \(\mu=\gamma_d^{\otimes r}\), where \(\gamma_j=N(0,I_j)\). The actual row is \(\Phi_i(\omega)=(\omega_{1,i},\ldots,\omega_{r,i})\). No row law or mean is supplied by the caller.

Put \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\), \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(t_i[0]=1\), and \(t_i[k]=\sqrt2\cos(k\theta_i)\) for \(1\le k\le q\). The source physical index is \(i.val+1\); feature indices remain \(k.val\).

The common scalar is fixed by \(a=r^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R^r}\|x\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\|x\|^2\le L\}}\,d\gamma_r(x)\). Its retained-radius integrability belongs to the reused canonical moment proof. The actual row law identifies this same scalar in every physical row; no free per-row coefficient is introduced.

The displayed \(Y_i\) uses its own inclusive local cutoff, inverse-\(d\) scaling, and Gaussian-first paired indices in the Kronecker product. It is an unconditional truncated matrix on the same original \(\mu\); the law is not conditioned on all rows passing.

Matrix expectations are complete Bochner integrals in the actual finite-dimensional Euclidean operator norm. Integrability of every \(Y_i\) and of both actual sums is proved. The source displays sums of expectations; finite integrability and integral exchange internally give the displayed actual-sum expectations. No independence, Gram, moment, integrability, mean, \(\tau\), or condition-number certificate is a premise.

theorem actual_source_truncated_matrix_means
    {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let a : ℝ :=
    (∫ x : E, Set.indicator {y : E | ‖y‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} (fun y : E => ‖y‖ ^ 2) x
      ∂stdGaussian E) / r
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (Y i) μ) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin d, (∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ) =
      (a / (d : ℝ)) • Matrix.kronecker
        (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
:= by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let a : ℝ :=
    (∫ x : E, Set.indicator {y : E | ‖y‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} (fun y : E => ‖y‖ ^ 2) x
      ∂stdGaussian E) / r
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let ν : Measure E := stdGaussian E
  let M := Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let N := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let good : Set E := {x | ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L}
  let G : E → M := fun x => Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp x) (WithLp.ofLp x)
  let kept : E → M := good.indicator G
  have moment := FixedSpectrumTruncatedRowMoment.actual_truncated_row_second_moment
    (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change Integrable kept ν ∧ (∫ x, kept x ∂ν) = a • (1 : M) at moment
  have row_law (i : Fin d) : MeasurePreserving (row i) μ ν :=
    FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw.actual_source_row_marginal_law hq i
  have actual_kept_integrable (i : Fin d) :
      Integrable (fun ω => kept (row i ω)) μ :=
    (row_law i).integrable_comp_of_integrable moment.1
  have actual_kept_mean (i : Fin d) :
      (∫ ω, kept (row i ω) ∂μ) = a • (1 : M) := by
    have measurable_on_map : AEStronglyMeasurable kept (Measure.map (row i) μ) := by
      rw [(row_law i).map_eq]
      exact moment.1.aestronglyMeasurable
    have transport := integral_map (row_law i).measurable.aemeasurable measurable_on_map
    rw [(row_law i).map_eq] at transport
    exact transport.symm.trans moment.2
  let feature : Fin d → M := fun i => Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i)
  let tensor : Fin d → M →ₗ[ℝ] N := fun i =>
    (Matrix.kroneckerBilinear : M →ₗ[ℝ] M →ₗ[ℝ] N).flip (feature i)
  let scaled : Fin d → M →L[ℝ] N := fun i => (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • (tensor i).toContinuousLinearMap
  have actual_image (i : Fin d) : Y i = fun ω => scaled i (kept (row i ω)) := by
    funext ω
    change (if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (G (row i ω)) (feature i) else 0) =
        (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (kept (row i ω)) (feature i)
    by_cases hω : ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L
    · simp [hω, kept, good]
    · simp [hω, kept, good]
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (Y i) μ) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin d, (∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ) =
      (a / (d : ℝ)) • Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (feature i)
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    rw [actual_image]
    exact (scaled i).integrable_comp (actual_kept_integrable i)
  · intro i
    calc
      (∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ) = scaled i (∫ ω, kept (row i ω) ∂μ) := by
        rw [actual_image]
        exact (scaled i).integral_comp_comm (actual_kept_integrable i)
      _ = scaled i (a • (1 : M)) := congrArg (scaled i) (actual_kept_mean i)
      _ = a • scaled i (1 : M) := (scaled i).map_smul a (1 : M)
      _ = (a / (d : ℝ)) • Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (feature i) := by
        change a • ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (feature i)) = _
        simp only [smul_smul, div_eq_mul_inv]

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixMean

  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))

    (∫ x : E, Set.indicator {y : E | ‖y‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} (fun y : E => ‖y‖ ^ 2) x
      ∂stdGaussian E) / r
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then

        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))

    Integrable (fun ω => ∑ i : Fin d,
      Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i) • Y i ω) μ ∧
    (∫ ω, ∑ i : Fin d, Y i ω ∂μ) =
      a • (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) ∧
    (∫ ω, ∑ i : Fin d, Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i) • Y i ω ∂μ) = 0
:= by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let a : ℝ :=
    (∫ x : E, Set.indicator {y : E | ‖y‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} (fun y : E => ‖y‖ ^ 2) x
      ∂stdGaussian E) / r
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)

    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let M := Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let N := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let w : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i)
  let feature : Fin d → M := fun i => Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i)
  let tensor : M →ₗ[ℝ] N :=
    (Matrix.kroneckerBilinear : M →ₗ[ℝ] M →ₗ[ℝ] N) (1 : M)
  let K : Fin d → N := fun i => tensor (feature i)
  have moments := FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixMean.actual_source_truncated_matrix_means
    (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (Y i) μ) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, (∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ) = (a / (d : ℝ)) • K i) at moments
  have half_grid (i : Fin d) :
      ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ) = θ i := by
    dsimp only [θ]
    ring
  have frame := FixedSpectrumCosineGram.actual_cosine_frame_gram (d := d) (q := q) hq
  dsimp only at frame
  simp_rw [half_grid] at frame
  change t.transpose * t = (d : ℝ) • (1 : M) ∧
    t.transpose * Matrix.diagonal w * t = 0 ∧ _ at frame
  have gram : (∑ i : Fin d, feature i) = (d : ℝ) • (1 : M) := by
    ext j k

        Matrix.sum_apply j k Finset.univ feature

        simpa only [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply] using
          congrFun (congrFun frame.1 j) k
  have weighted_gram : (∑ i : Fin d, w i • feature i) = 0 := by
    ext j k
    have weighted_entry := congrFun (congrFun frame.2.1 j) k
    change (∑ i : Fin d, (t.transpose * Matrix.diagonal w) j i * t i k) = 0 at weighted_entry
    simp only [Matrix.mul_diagonal, Matrix.transpose_apply] at weighted_entry
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin d, w i • feature i) j k = ∑ i : Fin d, w i * (t i j * t i k) :=
        Matrix.sum_apply j k Finset.univ (fun i => w i • feature i)
      _ = ∑ i : Fin d, t i j * w i * t i k := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro i _
        ring
      _ = (0 : M) j k := weighted_entry

reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), including zero whenever consistent with the following inequality, assume
\[
2q+1<d.
\]
Everything defined below is fixed by this pair \((d,q)\). There are no further hypotheses. In particular, \(q\geq0\), \(d\geq2q+2\), and \(d>0\). Put \(r=q+1\), using the same number as an integer dimension and its usual real embedding in scalar formulas. Thus \(r\geq1\).

The index set \(\operatorname{Fin}(d)\) is \(\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), and \(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\) is \(\{0,\ldots,q\}\). Let
\[
D=\mathbb R^d,\qquad E=\mathbb R^{q+1},\qquad
\Omega=\{\omega:\{0,\ldots,q\}\longrightarrow\mathbb R^d\}.
\]
Both Euclidean spaces carry their Euclidean norms and Borel measurable structures; \(\Omega\) carries the finite product measurable structure. For any such Euclidean space \(V\), write \(\gamma_V\) for its centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance. The probability measure on \(\Omega\) is
\[
\mu=\bigotimes_{b=0}^{q}\gamma_D.
\]
The probability experiment is therefore to draw \(q+1\) independent standard Gaussian vectors \(\omega(0),\ldots,\omega(q)\) in \(\mathbb R^d\). Equivalently, writing \(\omega_{b,i}\) for coordinate \(i\) of vector \(\omega(b)\), one draws the \((q+1)d\) independent real standard Gaussian coordinates \(\omega_{b,i}\), with \(0\leq b\leq q\) and \(0\leq i<d\).

Define the deterministic real threshold and coefficient
\[
L=2(q+1)+3\log(1000d)
\]
and
\[
a=\frac{1}{q+1}
  \int_{\mathbb R^{q+1}}
     \mathbf 1_{\{y:\|y\|_2^2\leq L\}}(x)\,\|x\|_2^2
     \,d\gamma_E(x).
\]
Here \(\log\) is the natural logarithm, and
\(\|x\|_2^2=\sum_{b=0}^{q}x_b^2\).
The indicator makes the scalar integrand equal to \(\|x\|_2^2\) when \(\|x\|_2^2\leq L\) and equal to zero otherwise. The boundary is included. This formula defines a particular canonical number \(a\) from \(d\) and \(q\); \(a\) is not an arbitrary input, a supplied certificate, or an additional assumption. Its integral is with respect to a separate standard Gaussian variable in \(E\). All integrals in this statement are Bochner integrals under the supplied convention that the integral is totalized to zero outside complete or integrable cases. The displayed scalar definition is a fixed definition, not a separately stated integrability hypothesis or conclusion.

For every coordinate index \(i\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), define
\[
\theta_i=\frac{(i+\tfrac12)\pi}{d}.
\]
Define a deterministic real vector \(t_i\) indexed by \(k\in\{0,\ldots,q\}\) by
\[
(t_i)_k=
\begin{cases}
1,& k=0,\\
\sqrt{2}\cos(k\theta_i),& k\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\pi\) is the usual circle constant, and \(\sqrt{2}\) is the nonnegative square root of \(2\). Indices appearing in these scalar formulas are embedded from natural numbers into real numbers.

For each \(i\) and each outcome \(\omega\), form the row vector
\[
g_i(\omega)=(\omega_{0,i},\omega_{1,i},\ldots,\omega_{q,i})\in E,
\qquad
s_i(\omega)=\|g_i(\omega)\|_2^2
            =\sum_{b=0}^{q}\omega_{b,i}^2.
\]
The coordinate wrapping and unwrapping in the packet merely regard this coordinate function as a Euclidean vector and recover the same real coordinates. Define the random matrix \(Y_i(\omega)\) of size \((q+1)^2\times(q+1)^2\), with rows and columns indexed by pairs in \(\{0,\ldots,q\}\times\{0,\ldots,q\}\), by
\[
Y_i(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac1d\bigl(g_i(\omega)g_i(\omega)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)
                   \otimes\bigl(t_i t_i^{\mathsf T}\bigr),
     & s_i(\omega)\leq L,\\
0,&s_i(\omega)>L.
\end{cases}
\]
The zero in the second branch is the zero matrix. For coordinate vectors \(u,v\), the outer product \(uv^{\mathsf T}\) has entry \(u_bv_c\) in row \(b\), column \(c\). The Kronecker product uses the following order of paired indices: if \(A\) and \(B\) have indices in \(\{0,\ldots,q\}\), then
\[
(A\otimes B)_{(b,k),(c,\ell)}=A_{b,c}B_{k,\ell}.
\]
Scalar multiplication by \(1/d\) multiplies each matrix entry. Consequently the complete entry formula, for every \(b,c,k,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,q\}\), is
\[
\bigl(Y_i(\omega)\bigr)_{(b,k),(c,\ell)}
 =\frac1d\,
   \mathbf 1_{\{\omega:\sum_{j=0}^{q}\omega_{j,i}^2\leq L\}}(\omega)
   \,\omega_{b,i}\omega_{c,i}(t_i)_k(t_i)_\ell.
\]
Thus the random outputs specified by the proposition are the \(d\) matrices \(Y_i\), each obtained by setting its entire outer-product matrix to zero when its own row norm squared exceeds \(L\).

The conclusion is the conjunction of these two assertions:

1. For every \(i\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), the function \(Y_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{(q+1)^2\times(q+1)^2}\) is integrable with respect to \(\mu\). In the supplied meaning, it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and has finite integral of its extended norm, where the finite complete real matrix space uses the Euclidean operator norm. Equivalently, the norm condition is
   \[
   \int_\Omega \|Y_i(\omega)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,d\mu(\omega)<\infty.
   \]
   This is an asserted conclusion, not a premise.

2. For every \(i\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), its Bochner integral is exactly
   \[
   \int_\Omega Y_i(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)
      =\frac{a}{d}\left(I_{q+1}\otimes t_i t_i^{\mathsf T}\right),
   \]
   where \(I_{q+1}\) is the identity matrix on the first, Gaussian-coordinate index. In coordinates, for every \(b,c,k,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,q\}\), this says
   \[
   \int_\Omega
      \bigl(Y_i(\omega)\bigr)_{(b,k),(c,\ell)}\,d\mu(\omega)
      =\frac{a}{d}\,\delta_{b,c}\,(t_i)_k(t_i)_\ell,
   \]
   where \(\delta_{b,c}=1\) when \(b=c\), and \(\delta_{b,c}=0\) otherwise. The explicit integrability conclusion ensures that this displayed matrix integral is an actual integrable expectation.

Both assertions range over every coordinate index \(i\) for each admissible pair \((d,q)\). They are deterministic statements about the functions and their integrals under the specified product measure, rather than a sample-dependent success claim. They do not assert that the displayed expectation equals the sampled matrix, nor state a concentration bound, a success probability, or a conclusion about a sum of the matrices.

All normalizations and constants are fixed: \(r=q+1\), the threshold has coefficients \(2\), \(3\), and \(1000\), the feature normalization is \(\sqrt2\), the Gaussian truncated second moment is divided by \(q+1\), and both the sampled matrix and its expectation have the factor \(1/d\). There is no unspecified constant or certificate dependence. The objects \(D,E,\Omega,\mu,r,L,a,\theta,t,g,Y\) depend only on \(d,q\), their indicated indices, and (where applicable) the outcome \(\omega\). The coefficient \(a\) is common to all \(i\).

The literal natural-number quantification permits \(q=0\). In that case the only feature index and Gaussian-vector index are zero, \(r=1\), the assumption is \(1<d\), \((t_i)_0=1\), and \(Y_i\) is the one-by-one matrix with entry
\[
\frac1d\,\mathbf 1_{\{\omega:\omega_{0,i}^2\leq 2+3\log(1000d)\}}(\omega)
\,\omega_{0,i}^2.
\]
The same two conclusions apply, with expectation the one-by-one matrix \([a/d]\) and with \(a\) given by the stated one-dimensional canonical Gaussian integral. Values \(d=0\) and \(d=1\) satisfy no instance of the hypothesis, so they yield no additional cases.
